fr:mainmatter.fr:p: In Wrong Definition of FollowLast, I mention that the definition of follow last sets in the Agda formalization needs to be changed to match the definitions used in [krishnaswami_typed_2019] and [bruggemannkleinwood].
Instead I had define follow last sets as

The followlast set (\mathsf {FLast}(\cdot )) of a grammar A are all the characters that may follow a word in the language of A in a string that is in the language of A.
\mathsf {FLast}(A) = \{ c ~|~ \exists w , w_A . w_A \in L(A) \land w_Acw \in L(A) \}
This definition is encoded in Dependent Lambek Calculus as follows,

fr:title.text: FollowLast Sets in Dependent Lambek Calculus

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: FollowLast Sets in Dependent Lambek Calculus

fr:mainmatter.fr:p:
The followlast set of a grammar A may be captured in Dependent Lambek Calculus via the following proposition:
c \not \in \mathsf {FLast}(A) := A \And (A \otimes \texttt {"}c\texttt {"} \otimes \top ) \vdash \bot

It turns out the original definitions I used aren't incorrect, instead the follow last set of a disjunction must be augmented. In A typed, algebraic approach to parsing and Deterministic regular languages, the follow last sets of a disjunction obey a very aesthetic equality, \mathsf {FLast}(A \oplus B) = \mathsf {FLast}(A) \cup \mathsf {FLast}(B)
However, with my augmented definition if either of A or B is nullable, the follow last set of A \oplus B must also be unioned with \mathsf {First}(A) \cup \mathsf {First}(B).

fr:mainmatter.fr:p: Until now I had been using the wrong definition of follow last sets. Rather than what I intially had,

The followlast set (\mathsf {FLast}(\cdot )) of a grammar A are all the characters that may follow a word in the language of A in a string that is in the language of A.
\mathsf {FLast}(A) = \{ c ~|~ \exists w , w_A . w_A \in L(A) \land w_Acw \in L(A) \}
I should instead require w_A to be empty in \mathsf {FLast}(A) = \{ c ~|~ \exists w , w_A . w_A \in L(A) \setminus \{ \epsilon \} \land w_A c w \in L(A) \}

Or at least that's what they have in Neel's paper. Max believes I should have a more compelling argument for which definition is better/more appropriate, which is fair enough. The best argument I have thus far is that our original definition would break the property that \mathsf {FLast}(A \oplus B) = \mathsf {FLast}(A) \cup \mathsf {FLast}(B)
